study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Liu et al., Progress in Neuropsychopharmacology & Biological Psychiatry, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Individualized functional connectome abnormalities obtained using two normative model unveil neurophysiological subtypes of obsessive compulsive disorder

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study recruited participants from a single site: the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University in China. Healthy controls (n=104) were enlisted from the community via poster advertisements, and OCD patients (n=99) were recruited from outpatient services within the Department of Psychiatry. All participants were of Han Chinese ethnicity.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "A total of ninety-eight first-episode and untreated patients diagnosed with OCD were recruited from outpatient services within the Department of Psychiatry at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University." ... "Healthy controls (HCs, n = 104) were enlisted from the community via poster advertisements."

answer.SINGLE-SITE (HCs): normative model training (via 10-fold cross-validation) and application to patients

answer.SINGLE-SITE (OCD patients): clinical application - individualized deviation calculation and subtype identification

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The healthy controls (n=104) were used to train the Gaussian process regression normative models for functional connectivity strength (FCS) using 10-fold cross-validation. The trained models were then applied to OCD patients (n=99) to calculate individualized FCS abnormalities (Z-scores), which were subsequently used as features for k-means clustering to identify OCD subtypes.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "First, we evaluated the performance of the Gaussian process regression model in predicting FCS values within HCs through 10-fold cross-validation." ... "Subsequently, for each brain region, a Gaussian process regression model was trained to estimate the normative range of FCS values as a function of age and sex within HCs. This model was then applied to each patient, yielding a predicted FCS value."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using 104 healthy controls. The model was trained and validated using 10-fold cross-validation within the HC sample. No separate train/test split numbers are explicitly reported; cross-validation was performed on the entire HC dataset.
